results.title: SNR definition in MRIQC - mriqc - Neurostars
results.content:
Title: SNR definition in MRIQC - mriqc - Neurostars
# SNR definition in MRIQC. I have a question about SNR definition in MRIQC. According to MRIQC documentation, under the tab “mriqc.qc.anatomical.snr(*mu\_fg*, *sigma\_fg*, *n*)”, SNR is calculated as ratio between the mean of the foreground and the standard deviation of the same region. Tracula, a software to analyze DWI, provides SNR as the ratio between the mean of the white matter and the standard deviation of the same white matter. So the definition is in line with the formula in MRIQC summary. However, at the same link of MRI documentation, in the formulas from the article “Magnotta et al, 2006” and from Table 2 in the article “Esteban et al, 2017” (used as reference articles), SNR is mentioned as ratio between the mean of the foreground and the standard deviation of air (=background). Actually as you have noticed, there are 2 SNR definitions used in MRIQC:. But there are even more definitions out there! D. Measuring Signal-to-Noise Ratio in Partially Parallel Imaging MRI: Signal-to-Noise Ratio in Parallel Imaging MRI. R. Image Reconstruction in SNR Units: A General Method for SNR Measurement. O. Measurement of Signal-to-Noise Ratios in MR Images: Influence of Multichannel Coils, Parallel Imaging, and Reconstruction Filters. On the Definition of Signal-To-Noise Ratio and Contrast-To-Noise Ratio for FMRI Data. On the Definition of Signal-To-Noise Ratio and Contrast-To-Noise Ratio for fMRI Data. Obviously it is important to stick to the same definition if you want to compare images. Thank you for your answer (and your welcome!). Are you calculating the SNR on T1w images? Alternative methods that rely on measurement of noise from regions of interest in the signal-free background (1,2) are not appropriate for parallel imaging where the noise level is highly variable across the field-of-view. The conventionally determined SNR based on separate signal and noise regions in a single image will in general not agree with the true SNR measured in images after the application of certain reconstruction filters, multichannel reconstruction, or parallel imaging. I am indeed checking SNR on T1W images (and DTI images, too). `snr_total` or `snrd_total` seem to be calculated in the union of WM, GM and CSF masks:. self._results["snr"][tlabel] = snrvals[-1]. self._results["snr"]["total"] = float(np.mean(snrvals)).

results.content:
Title: MRIQC - Scaling of voxel-wise average maps in DWI pipeline (Siemens vs Philips) - Software Support - Neurostars
# MRIQC - Scaling of voxel-wise average maps in DWI pipeline (Siemens vs Philips). I’ve run MRIQC via Docker (`nipreps/mriqc:latest; v25.1.0.dev45+g699d1691`) on a DWI dataset which has been acquired on a Siemens Prisma 3T and a Philips Achieva 3T scanner. `nipreps/mriqc:latest; v25.1.0.dev45+g699d1691`. When inspecting the DWI-HTML-reports I noticed that the voxel-wise average maps show a reversed scale (Philips bright brain, dark background; Siemens: dark brain, bright background; see below), which was consistent across all shells and participants. I’ve also acquired resting-state fMRI scans. Here the scaling is not reversed in the voxel-wise average of the BOLD timeseries. vw-avg-map\_philvssiem1218×744 120 KB. Consequently QC-metrics which are based on the background values (e.g. FBER) show a huge difference when comparing the two scanner sites. When checking the raw DICOM and NIfTI data, I noticed that in the Philips datasets, the signal intensity outside the skull was 0, whereas in the Siemens datasets, it was ~300 in the b=0 volumes. I’m wondering if someone else has experienced this behaviour of MRIQC when using different scanners and how I should proceed the quality assessment of my dataset. results.title: A multi-modal neuroimaging data release for Meige Syndrome and Facial Paralysis Research | Scientific Data
results.content: Through incorporating patients with facial paralysis and Meige syndrome into our study and amalgamating their data into a shared database, we aim to enrich the comprehension of these disorders and bolster future research and advancements in related neuroscientific domains. Quality assessments on the FP rfMRI data using both bar (the left column) and scatter (the right column) plots of the following quality metrics: (**a**) Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) (**b**) Foreground to Background Energy Ratio (FBER) (**c**) Entropy Focus Criteria (EFC) (**d**) Full-Width Half Maximum (FWHM), (**e**) Mean Framewise Displacement (FD\_MEAN), (**f**) Derivative of time series and root-mean-square VARiance over voxelS (DVARS), (**g**) Global Correlation (GCOR). Quality assessments on the HC rfMRI data using both bar (the left column) and scatter (the right column) plots of the following quality metrics: (**a**) Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) (**b**) Foreground to Background Energy Ratio (FBER) (**c**) Entropy Focus Criteria (EFC) (**d**) Full-Width Half Maximum (FWHM), (**e**) Mean Framewise Displacement (FD\_MEAN), (**f**) Derivative of time series and root-mean-square VARiance over voxelS (DVARS), (**g**) Global Correlation (GCOR). Quality assessments on the MEIGE sMRI data using both bar (the left column) and scatter (the right column) plots of the following quality metrics: (**a**) Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) (**b**) Foreground to Background Energy Ratio (FBER) (**c**) Contrast-to-Noise Ratio (CNR) (**d**) Entropy Focus Criteria (EFC) (**e**) Full-Width Half Maximum (FWHM). Quality assessments on the HC rfMRI data using both bar (the left column) and scatter (the right column) plots of the following quality metrics: (**a**) Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) (**b**) Foreground to Background Energy Ratio (FBER) (**c**) Entropy Focus Criteria (EFC) (**d**) Full-Width Half Maximum (FWHM), (**e**) Mean Framewise Displacement (FD\_MEAN), (**f**) Derivative of time series and root-mean-square VARiance over voxelS (DVARS), (**g**) Global Correlation (GCOR). Our objective is to persist in data accumulation, aiming to augment and diversify the existing repository, which in turn will catalyze further research advancements in the domain of Meige syndrome, facial paralysis, and associated neurological disorders.In summation, our study is characterized by stringent adherence to data consistency, achieved through the use of a standardized imaging modality and consistent scanning parameters.
